Visit note | 2025-04-15 04:00 PM | Dr. Nusrat Jahan, General Medicine | Patient: Mehedi Shikder, 52, male. Mr. Shikder states he has pain behind his eyes, a faint rash on his arms, and severe aching in his bones and muscles. He mentions this started during the monsoon after mosquitoes bred in water tanks near Rangpur. He works as a tailor and has Type 2 diabetes mellitus. He reports no bleeding or breathing difficulty. On examination: temperature 102.0°F, BP 121/79 mmHg, pulse 95 bpm, weight 85 kg, platelet count 75000 per microlitre. Chest is clear and abdomen is soft. Assessment: Dengue fever. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to drink at least three litres of fluid a day, avoid ibuprofen and aspirin, repeat the platelet count in 48 hours, and go to hospital at once for bleeding gums, black stools, or severe belly pain. Follow-up in 48 hours with a repeat platelet count.
